sources.entry: Verdaccio | Lightweight private npm proxy registry

summary.one_liner: Verdaccio is a lightweight, zero-config private npm registry that can also proxy and cache public registries such as npmjs.org.
summary.what_it_does: Verdaccio runs as a local npm registry with its own built-in small database, so no external database is needed to start. It can host private packages that are published and installed like public ones. It can proxy other registries (such as npmjs.org) and cache downloaded modules, and it can chain multiple registries behind one endpoint via uplinks. Packages can be overridden by publishing a locally modified version under the same name. Storage can be extended with community plugins for services such as Amazon S3 and Google Cloud Storage, or with custom plugins built using a Yeoman generator. The README says npm commands such as publish, install, unpublish, dist-tag, deprecate, adduser, token, search, ping and audit are supported, and that yarn and pnpm are tested in CI.
use_cases: host private npm packages inside a company
cache npmjs.org packages for multiple servers
run a private registry for end-to-end testing in CI
override a third-party npm package with a local fix
chain multiple npm registries behind one endpoint
publish internal packages without sending code to a public registry
how_to_run: npm set registry <url>  (optional, points npm at the local registry)
notable: Zero-config startup with a built-in small database; no external DB needed
Proxies and caches npmjs.org and can chain multiple uplink registries
Plugin ecosystem for storage backends such as S3 and Google Cloud Storage
Fast enough to boot in seconds, used for end-to-end testing in many open source projects
Official Docker image and Helm chart
caveats: The README says it does not currently support PM2 cluster mode and may behave unexpectedly with it
This master branch (Version Next) requires Node.js 24 or higher; Version 6 requires Node.js 22 or higher
Some npm features are not fully covered, since the README says support is not always possible
keywords: share npm packages with my team
